summary: Jan Niecisław Baudouin de Courtenay was a linguist who studied at Warsaw, Charles, Berlin, Leipzig under August Leskien, and Jagiellonian universities. He held posts at Kazan, Tartu, Jagiellonian, St. Petersburg, Warsaw, and the Catholic University of Lublin.

Jan P. Hogendijk is an Indologist and historian who earned his doctorate at Utrecht University. His career includes posts at Brown, Frankfurt, Utrecht, Leiden, the University of Tehran, and King Fahd University of Petroleum and Minerals.

Jan Peter F. Hintelmann works in Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Hamburg under doctoral supervisor Marianne Pieper and studied under traditional teachers Thupten Nyandak, Tenzin Kunga, Sonam Senge, and Geshe Sonam Rinchen.

Jan Westerhoff works in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He studied at Cambridge under Michael Potter and at SOAS. His academic posts include positions at Oxford, SOAS, Durham, the City University of New York, and Columbia University.

Jan Willem de Jong was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar. He studied at Leiden, Harvard, the Sorbonne, and Collège de France under Walter Eugene Clark, Paul Demiéville, and F. B. J. Kuiper. He held posts at Leiden and Harvard.

Jan-Ulrich Sobisch works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under David P. Jackson, David Seyfort Ruegg, and Nubpa Rinpoche. He held posts at the University of Copenhagen, the University of Hamburg, the University of Munich, and the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project.
Janakiballav Bhattacharyya worked in Indology and philosophy, studying under Surendranath Dasgupta. He held an attested post at Jadavpur University in 1977.
Janardan Mishra worked in Indology and philosophy. He held the post of Director at the Mithila Institute of Post-Graduate Studies and Research in Sanskrit Learning, attested in 1959 and 1987.
Jane Bunnag is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at the University of London by 1969, studying under supervisors E. Michael Mendelson and Barbara E. Ward.
Jane Caple works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. She held a post at the University of Leeds and is attested as a Research Fellow at the University of Manchester in 2026.

Jane Ellen Harrison was a scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology. She studied at Cheltenham Ladies' College and Newnham College under Robert Alexander Neil, and later held a post at the University of Cambridge from roughly 1898 to 1922.

Jane-Marie Law is a scholar of religious studies and Japanology. She held positions at Cornell University, serving as Director of Graduate Studies (attested 2008) and Associate Professor (attested 2026).

Janet Gyatso is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who completed her BA, MA, and PhD at UC Berkeley. She held academic posts at Stony Brook, Wesleyan, Amherst College, the University of Michigan, and Harvard University.

Janet R. Goodwin works in Japanology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. She studied at UC Berkeley under Delmer M. Brown and Britten Dean, and held attested positions in 1994 at the University of Southern California and the University of Aizu.
Jang-Kil Chun is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under teachers Paul J. Griffiths, Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Frances Wilson, and doctoral supervisor Minoru Kiyota.

Janice Dean Willis is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She studied at Cornell and Columbia under Alex Wayman and Thubten Yeshe. She was a professor at Wesleyan University (1977–2013) and taught at Agnes Scott College (2014–2020).

Janice Leoshko is a scholar of history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She studied under doctoral supervisor Susan L. Huntington and is attested as Professor Emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin in 2026.

Jann Ronis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under David Germano, also studying under Jeffrey Hopkins and Sonam Tenpa, and held an attested post there in 2007.

Jared Rhoton was a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under teacher Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga and completed his dissertation at Columbia University under doctoral supervisor Alex Wayman by 1985.

Jarl Charpentier was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Uppsala University under Karl Ferdinand Johansson and at the University of Bonn under Hermann Jacobi. He served as Assistant Professor, Deputy Professor, and Professor at Uppsala University.
